sections.h2: Who collects property tax on a house inside Cleveland city limits?
sections.html:
A house inside Cleveland gets two separate tax bills, one from the City of Cleveland and one from Bradley County. The county Assessor of Property values the parcel for both, the Bradley County Trustee collects the county bill, and the city's finance office collects the city bill.

  • City of Cleveland Finance: Municipal Building, 190 Church Street NE, open 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday. Phone (423) 472-4551. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1519.
  • Bradley County Trustee: 1701 Keith Street NW, phone (423) 728-7247. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Friday. Tim Akins took the office after the 2026 election.
  • Bradley County Assessor of Property: (423) 728-7126, for address changes, values and appeals.

The county also takes calls on its toll-free automated payment line at (833) 591-7276.

sections.h2: When do Cleveland tax bills come due and when does interest start?
sections.html:
Cleveland bills for the current calendar year go out in the first week of October, and the tax is due from October 1 through February 28 of the next year without penalty. If payment is not received or postmarked by February 28, a 1.5 percent charge is added on the first of March and again each month after that.

The city's own page says that charge keeps building to a cap of 18 percent, which takes twelve months. After that, unpaid taxes pass to the Bradley County Clerk and Master. The Trustee's page asks owners to pay county tax by the end of February as well.

sections.h2: What is the Cleveland and Bradley County tax rate?
sections.html:
Bradley County's net property tax rate for 2025 is .9922 per $100 of assessed value. The Trustee's FAQ shows two fire district surcharges that apply only to county-only properties: .2182 inside the fire fringe and .2408 outside it, which would not apply to a house inside Cleveland.

The Trustee does not publish the city rate on its FAQ and directs owners to the city office at (423) 472-4551, so ask for the current Cleveland rate when estimating a bill. Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value across Tennessee, so on a house appraised at $272,200, the Census Bureau's median owner-occupied value for Cleveland, the assessed value would be $68,050. At the county's .9922 rate, that produces about $675 in county tax before any city amount.

sections.h2: What relief exists for Cleveland homeowners who struggle with the bill?
sections.html:
Bradley County runs the state Tax Relief program through the Trustee's office, and it also runs its own Tax Freeze for owners 65 and older. The City Clerk's office can take state relief applications at the Municipal Building as well.

  • Tax Relief reimburses part of the tax for elderly or disabled owners who live in the home. For 2025 the county brochure listed up to $81 for Cleveland city residents, $99 inside the fire fringe and $101 outside it.
  • Tax Freeze was adopted by the Bradley County Commission in August 2007. It holds the tax at the amount for the first year the owner qualifies, as long as the owner stays eligible and makes no improvements.
  • Disabled veterans and surviving spouses can qualify for relief paid on the first $175,000 of home market value.

All taxes must be paid and current before relief is granted. The 2025 application deadline was April 5, 2026, so ask the Trustee for the 2026 deadline and income limit.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Cleveland property valuation?
sections.html:
Call the Bradley County Assessor of Property at (423) 728-7126 and ask for an informal review. The Assessor's appraisal staff look at the file first, and a disagreement can go to the Board of Equalization, a panel of local citizens.

The city's finance page notes that appeals can be started at any time but are heard in the spring, and a decision affects only that year's tax. The Tennessee Comptroller states that county boards usually convene on June 1 and that an appeal to the county board keeps the right to go on to the State Board of Equalization.

sections.h2: What happens if Cleveland property tax is never paid?
sections.html:
The Bradley County Clerk and Master runs the annual tax sale on delinquent parcels, and the Trustee's office does not keep a mailing list. The county says sales are open public auctions, the notice list is published two to three weeks before the sale, and the price is paid in cash, money order or check at the time of sale.

A sale clears every lien except state and federal liens. The buyer cannot take possession until one year after the confirmation of sale is filed, and during that time the former owner can redeem. The buyer earns 10 percent a year during the redemption period. Contact the Clerk and Master at (423) 728-7209 for the next sale.

sections.h2: What should a Cleveland seller know about the local housing stock?
sections.html:
Cleveland is the Bradley County seat and the largest city in the county. It was incorporated on February 4, 1842, and the Census Bureau counted 47,356 residents in 2020 and estimated 51,172 in July 2025. The city covers about 27 square miles of land.

The terrain is a series of parallel ridges, including Candies Creek Ridge, that extend the Appalachians north to south. Interstate 75 passes through the west side with three exits, and the APD-40 beltway with Paul Huff Parkway serves the north. Lee University and Cleveland State Community College are both in the city, and Cleveland City Schools serves students living inside the city limits while Bradley County Schools covers the rest of the county.

Manufacturing anchors the local economy. Whirlpool, Mars, Procter and Gamble and Duracell are among the employers listed for the area. The Census Bureau reports 18,829 households for 2020 to 2024, a median household income of $58,559 and a mean commute of 21.3 minutes. Only 48.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and median gross rent is $1,034, so a Cleveland house is more likely than in most Tennessee cities to be sold with a tenant in it.

sections.h2: How should a Cleveland seller deal with tax owed at closing?
sections.html:
Bradley County tells new owners to read the closing statement and ask the title company who pays the tax, because payment depends on the transfer date and unpaid taxes continue to accrue against the property. Ask the title company to pull both the county and city tax status before the contract date.

Cleveland's online system lets anyone verify that the current tax is paid, and the city office can supply a duplicate bill at (423) 472-4551. City partial payment agreements and payment plans only work if the balance is cleared before March, so a seller on one of those plans should ask the title company for a payoff figure instead of assuming the remaining installments transfer.

faqs.q: When is Cleveland property tax due?
faqs.a: Cleveland city tax is due from October 1 through February 28 of the following year without penalty. From March 1 a 1.5 percent monthly charge is added, up to 18 percent.

faqs.q: Who do I pay for property tax in Cleveland, TN?
faqs.a: Pay the City of Cleveland for the city tax and the Bradley County Trustee for the county tax. The city finance office is at 190 Church Street NE and the Trustee is at 1701 Keith Street NW.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Cleveland property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, with limits. The city accepts partial payments if you complete forms and pay the whole amount before March 1, and it offers a twelve month plan if forms are in by February 15. Online card payments carry a 3 percent fee.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Cleveland property value?
faqs.a: Call the Bradley County Assessor of Property at (423) 728-7126. If the review does not satisfy you, the Board of Equalization hears appeals in the spring.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Cleveland property tax?
faqs.a: Interest builds at 1.5 percent a month up to 18 percent, then the debt moves to the Bradley County Clerk and Master. Delinquent parcels can be sold at a public auction with a one year redemption period.
